title: COOP$^2$: Defining, Observing, and Repairing Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
claim: A two-layer interface couples symbolic agent communication with grounded environment execution, with task constraints diagnosing failures and feeding repair signals back.
layout: Top two layer boxes with arrows between; bottom MAEIL timeline and task-design panels; feedback arrow
description: A dense system diagram. The top left box, Layer I: Cognitive (symbolic), shows cartoon robots with speech bubbles for planning, interrupting and replanning, and a looping purple arrow. The top right box, Layer II: Primitive, holds active plans, an environment/task update step with game screenshots, and primitive multi-agent execution with agent actions a_{i,t}. It also shows the MA-CRAFTER and CUBE environments and a looping blue arrow. Two large pink and blue arrows between the layers carry formulas for plan activity and messages. The bottom left, Agent with MAEIL, shows a legend (ready, terminate, resume, send, receive) and colored timeline bars for agents. The bottom right, Task Design, shows participation and task-progress constraints, with green check and red cross examples for successful and failed joint actions. A pink 'Repair guide signal' arrow runs from the constraints back to Layer I. Green dashed lines link the task panels to the environments.
caption: Overview of COOP2. COOP2 models LLM-MAS through a cognitive–primitive interface (top) that couples a symbolic cognitive layer, where agents plan, communicate, interrupt, and replan through the Multi-Agent Environment Interaction Loop (MAEIL, bottom-left), with a primitive layer, where joint actions drive environment states and task-state transitions (sec. 3). Cooperative tasks, instantiated in MA-CRAFTER and CUBE, are guarded by participation and task-progress constraints; joint executions that satisfy all active constraints succeed while violations identify which cooperative requirements failed. These constraint signals support process-level diagnosis and feed COOP2-Repair (sec. 5), which opens targeted repair channels to revise plans before primitive execution.
abstract: Many complex tasks require extended effort, diverse capabilities, or coordinated actions beyond what a single agent can provide. However, simply adding more agents does not guarantee better performance, as effective cooperation depends on how agents interact with each other and with task structure to satisfy evolving constraints over time. This challenge is amplified for LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS): plans, messages, and revisions occur in natural language, whereas task progress depends on grounded environment actions. Current evaluations mostly treat cooperation as an implicit ingredient of final task success, leaving both cooperation and the effect of multi-agent interaction on task dynamics difficult to study. We introduce COOP$^2$, an evaluation framework that grounds high-level agent cooperation dynamics in LLM-MAS within task progress in the environment. COOP$^2$ then defines cooperative tasks with verifiable cooperative requirements, allowing us to analyze how cooperation unfolds over time with respect to task progress, as well as where and why cooperation breaks down. Building on this framework, we develop COOP$^2$-Repair, which predicts constraint failures from group plans and opens targeted repair channels for guided revisions. Across two environments and three communication structures, COOP$^2$-Repair improves task success and constraint satisfaction while exposing the additional decision overhead and communication load required for repair. The project web page can be found at: https://happyeureka.github.io/coop2.
